title.zh: 卷七十五 列傳第五: 耶律覿烈 耶律鐸臻 王郁 耶律圖魯窘
title.en: Volume 75 Biographies 5: Yelu Dilie, Yelu Duozhen, Wang Yu, Yelu Tulujiong
title.raw: 卷七十五 列傳第五: 耶律覿烈 耶律鐸臻 王郁 耶律圖魯窘 Volume 75 Biographies 5: Yelu Dilie, Yelu Duozhen, Wang Yu, Yelu Tulujiong

sentences.zh: 耶律覿烈

translations.literal: Yelu Dilie
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Dilie

sentences.zh: （羽之）〉

translations.literal: (Yuzhi))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Yuzhi))〉

sentences.zh: 耶律鐸臻

translations.literal: Yelu Duozhen
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Duozhen

sentences.zh: （古突呂不）〉

translations.literal: (Gu and Tulubu))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Gu and Tulubu))〉

sentences.zh: 王郁耶律圖魯窘

translations.literal: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong

sentences.zh: 羽之，小字兀裏，字寅底哂。

translations.literal: Yuzhi, childhood name Wuli, courtesy name Yindi Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi, whose childhood name was Wuli and whose courtesy name was Yindi Shen,

sentences.zh: 幼豪爽不群，長嗜學，通諸部語。

translations.literal: As a child he was bold and unorthodox; when grown he loved learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: was bold and unconventional as a youth; when grown he devoted himself to learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 太祖經營之初，多預軍謀。

translations.literal: In the early period of the Emperor Taizu's founding efforts, he took part in many military plans.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Taizu's state-building, he took part in many military plans.

sentences.zh: 天顯元年，渤海平，立皇太子為東丹王，以羽之為中臺省右次相。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxian, when Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan, and Yuzhi was made Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxian, after Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan and Yuzhi was appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.

sentences.zh: 時人心未安，左大相叠剌不逾月薨，羽之蒞事勤恪，威信並行。

translations.literal: At that time popular sentiment was still unsettled; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, but Yuzhi conducted affairs with diligence and strictness, and authority and trust went hand in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Popular sentiment was still unsettled at the time; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, yet Yuzhi handled affairs with diligence and rigor, and authority and trust went hand in hand.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，上表曰：「我大聖天皇始有東土，擇賢輔以撫斯民，不以臣愚而任之，國家利害，敢不以聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong acceded, he submitted a memorial saying: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first gained the eastern lands and chose worthy men to comfort the people. Though he did not regard this subject as wise, he still entrusted me with office; the gains and losses of the state—how dare I not report them?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Yuzhi submitted a memorial that read: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first secured the eastern lands and chose worthy ministers to govern the people. Though he did not regard me as capable, he still entrusted me with office; how could I fail to speak of what helps or harms the state?

sentences.zh: 渤海昔畏南朝，阻險自衛，居忽汗城。

translations.literal: Bohai in the past feared the Southern Court, relied on natural barriers for self-defense, and dwelt at Hohan city.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai once feared the Southern Court, held itself behind natural barriers, and made its seat at Hohan.

sentences.zh: 今去上京遼邈，既不為用，又不罷戍，果何為哉？

translations.literal: Now it lies far from the Supreme Capital; it is neither useful nor are the garrisons withdrawn—what purpose does this serve?
translations.idiomatic: It now lies far from the Supreme Capital, yet we neither put it to use nor withdraw the garrisons—what is the point?

sentences.zh: 先帝因彼離心，乘釁而動，故不戰而克。

translations.literal: The late emperor, because their hearts were divided, seized the opportunity and moved; therefore he conquered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor took advantage of their divided loyalties and struck when the moment was ripe, and so conquered them without a battle.

sentences.zh: 天授人與，彼一時也。

translations.literal: Heaven bestowed and men granted—that was a moment in time.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven granted the opportunity and men seized it—that was a moment that will not return.

sentences.zh: 遺種浸以蕃息，今居遠境，恐為後患。

translations.literal: The surviving people have gradually multiplied; now they dwell on distant borders and may become a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Their surviving people have gradually multiplied; living now on distant frontiers, they may yet become a future threat.

sentences.zh: 梁水之地，乃其故鄉，地衍土活，有木鐵鹽魚之利。

translations.literal: The land of Liangshui is their old homeland; the soil is broad and fertile, and there are advantages in timber, iron, salt, and fish.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangshui region is their ancestral homeland: the land is broad, the soil fertile, and it offers timber, iron, salt, and fish.

sentences.zh: 乘其微弱，徙還其民，萬世長策也。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their weakness, relocate their people back—a long-term policy for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: While they are still weak, move their people back home—that is a policy for the ages.

sentences.zh: 彼得故鄉，又獲木鐵鹽魚之饒，必安居樂業。

translations.literal: When they regain their homeland and also obtain the abundance of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle in peace and take joy in their work.
translations.idiomatic: Once they regain their homeland and the bounty of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle down and prosper.

sentences.zh: 然後選徒以翼吾左，突厥、党項、室韋夾輔吾右，可以坐制南邦，混一天下，成聖祖未集之功，貽後世無疆之福。

translations.literal: Then select settlers to strengthen our left flank; with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, we can control the southern states from a fixed position, unite all under Heaven, complete the unfinished work of the sage ancestor, and bequeath boundless blessings to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then choose settlers to strengthen our left, with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, and we can hold the southern states in check from a secure position, unite the realm, finish the work our sage founder left incomplete, and bequeath boundless blessings to posterity.

sentences.zh: 」表奏，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised it and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔徙東丹國民於梁水，時稱其善。

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered the people of Eastern Dan relocated to Liangshui; at the time his policy was praised as good.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict moved the people of Eastern Dan to Liangshui, and contemporaries praised the policy as wise.

sentences.zh: 人皇王奔唐，羽之鎮撫國人，一切如故。

translations.literal: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the people of the state and kept everything as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the populace and kept everything as it had been.

sentences.zh: 以功加守太傅，遷中臺省左相。

translations.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Acting Grand Tutor and transferred to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was additionally appointed Acting Grand Tutor and promoted to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.

sentences.zh: 會同初，以冊禮赴闕，加特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, he went to court for the investiture rites and was given the special advancement rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huitong era he went to court for the enthronement ceremonies and was granted the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 表奏左次相渤海蘇貪墨不法事，卒。

translations.literal: He memorialized reporting that Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, was corrupt and lawless, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial exposing the corruption and lawlessness of Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, then died.

sentences.zh: 子和裏，終東京留守。

translations.literal: His son Heli ended as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heli eventually served as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 耶律鐸臻，字敵輦，六院部人。

translations.literal: Yelu Duozhen, courtesy name Dinian, was a man of the Six Yuan Divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Duozhen, whose courtesy name was Dinian, came from the Six Yuan Divisions.

sentences.zh: 祖蒲古只，遙輦氏時再為本部夷離堇。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pugu Zhi twice served as Yilijin of this division in the time of the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pugu Zhi had twice served as tribal chieftain of their division under the Yaolian clan.

sentences.zh: 耶律狼德等既害玄祖，暴橫益肆。

translations.literal: After Yelu Langde and others had killed the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Yelu Langde and his faction murdered the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 蒲古只以計誘其黨，悉誅夷之。

translations.literal: Pugu Zhi by stratagem lured out their faction and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Zhi lured their faction into a trap by stratagem and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 鐸臻幼有誌節，太祖為於越，常居左右。

translations.literal: Duozhen in youth had resolve and integrity; when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, he constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Duozhen showed moral resolve even as a youth; while Emperor Taizu still held the title of Yuyue, he kept Duozhen constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 後即位，梁人遣使求轅軸材，太祖難之。

translations.literal: Later, when he took the throne, the people of Liang sent envoys requesting axle-hub timber, and the Emperor Taizu found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, Liang sent envoys requesting timber for chariot axles, and Emperor Taizu was at a loss how to respond.

sentences.zh: 鐸臻曰：「梁名求材，實覘吾輕重。

translations.literal: Duozhen said: "Liang asks for timber in name, but in fact they are probing our strength.
translations.idiomatic: Duozhen said, "Liang claims to want timber, but in truth they are testing our strength.

sentences.zh: 宜答曰：『材之所生，必深山窮谷，有神司之，須白鼻赤驢禱祠，然後可伐。

translations.literal: We should answer: 'Where the timber grows must be deep mountains and remote valleys; a spirit oversees it, and one must pray with a white-nosed red donkey before it can be cut.'
translations.idiomatic: We should answer that the timber grows only in deep mountains and remote valleys, that a spirit oversees it, and that it cannot be cut until one has prayed with a white-nosed red donkey.

sentences.zh: 』如此，則其語自塞矣。

translations.literal: ' In this way their words will choke themselves off.
translations.idiomatic: If we say that, their request will collapse of its own absurdity.

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " Before long it proved exactly so.
translations.idiomatic: " And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 天贊三年，將伐渤海，鐸臻諫曰：「陛下先事渤海，則西夏必躡吾後。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianzan, when he was about to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty deals with Bohai first, Western Xia will surely tread on our rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianzan, as the emperor prepared to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty strikes at Bohai first, Western Xia will surely fall upon our rear.

sentences.zh: 請先西討，庶無後顧憂。

translations.literal: Please attack west first, so that there may be no worry behind.
translations.idiomatic: Attack the west first, so that we need not fear what lies behind us.

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Taizu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及淳欽皇后稱制，惡鐸臻，囚之，誓曰：「鐵鎖朽，當釋汝！

translations.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, she disliked Duozhen, imprisoned him, and swore: "When the iron chains rot, I shall release you!
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, she took a dislike to Duozhen and imprisoned him, swearing, "When the iron chains rust through, I shall release you!

sentences.zh: 」既而召之，使者欲去鎖，鐸臻辭曰：「鐵未朽，可釋乎？

translations.literal: " Later she summoned him; the envoy wished to remove the locks, but Duozhen declined: "The iron has not rotted—may I be released?
translations.idiomatic: " Later she summoned him; when the messenger moved to remove his chains, Duozhen refused: "The iron has not yet rusted—may I be released?

sentences.zh: 」後聞，嘉嘆，趣召釋之。

translations.literal: " When she heard of this afterward, she praised and sighed, and urgently summoned and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " When she heard of this, she marveled and sighed with approval, and at once ordered him freed.

sentences.zh: 天顯二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tianxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianxian.

sentences.zh: 弟古、突呂不。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.

sentences.zh: 古，字涅剌昆，初名霞馬葛。

translations.literal: Gu, courtesy name Nielakun, original name Xiamage.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, whose courtesy name was Nielakun and whose original name was Xiamage,

sentences.zh: 太祖為於越，嘗從略地山右。

translations.literal: when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, once followed him in raiding the lands west of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Taizu was still Yuyue, once accompanied him in campaigns west of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 會李克用於雲州，古侍，克用異之曰：「是兒骨相非常，不宜使在左右。

translations.literal: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou; Gu attended him, and Keyong marveled, saying: "This boy's bone structure is extraordinary; he should not be kept at one's side.
translations.idiomatic: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou while attending the emperor; Keyong remarked in wonder, "This boy's bearing is extraordinary—he should not be kept close at hand.

sentences.zh: 」以故太祖頗忌之。

translations.literal: " For this reason the Emperor Taizu came to be somewhat wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: " For this reason Emperor Taizu grew somewhat wary of him.

sentences.zh: 時方西討，諸弟亂作，聞變，太祖問古與否，曰無。

translations.literal: At that time they were campaigning west; the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing of the disturbance, the Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu was involved; the answer was no.
translations.idiomatic: While the army was campaigning in the west, the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing the news, Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu had taken part; he was told no.

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「吾無患矣！

translations.literal: He rejoiced: "I have no worry!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced: "Then I have nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 」趣召古議。

translations.literal: " He urgently summoned Gu to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: He at once summoned Gu to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 古陳殄滅之策，後皆如言，以故錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Gu set forth a plan for their extermination; afterward events all matched his words, and for this reason rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Gu laid out a plan for their destruction, and events afterward unfolded exactly as he had said; for this the emperor lavished rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 神冊末，南伐，以古佐右皮室詳穩老古，與唐兵戰於雲碧店，老古中流矢，傷甚，太祖疑古陰害之。

translations.literal: At the end of Shence, on the southern campaign, Gu was made assistant to Laogu, Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang troops at Yunbi post, Laogu was struck by a flying arrow and badly wounded, and the Emperor Taizu suspected Gu of secretly harming him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Shence era, during the southern campaign, Gu served as deputy to Laogu, commander of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang forces at Yunbi, where Laogu was struck by an arrow and badly wounded. Emperor Taizu suspected that Gu had plotted against him in secret.

sentences.zh: 古知上意，跪曰：「陛下疑臣恥居老古麾下耶？

translations.literal: Gu knew the emperor's mind, knelt, and said: "Does Your Majesty suspect that this subject was ashamed to serve under Laogu?
translations.idiomatic: Gu understood the emperor's suspicion, knelt, and said, "Does Your Majesty think I was ashamed to serve under Laogu?

sentences.zh: 及今老古在，請遣使問之。

translations.literal: Since Laogu is still alive, please send an envoy to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Laogu is still alive—send someone to ask him.

sentences.zh: 」太祖使問老古，對曰：「臣於古無可疑者。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Taizu sent to ask Laogu, who answered: "This subject has nothing doubtful about Gu.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu did so; Laogu replied, "I have no suspicion of Gu whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 」上意乃釋。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's doubts were dispelled.

sentences.zh: 老古卒，遂以古為右皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: When Laogu died, Gu was then made Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division.
translations.idiomatic: After Laogu died, Gu was appointed commander of the Right Pishi Division.

sentences.zh: 既卒，太祖謂左右曰：「古死，猶長松自倒，非吾伐之也。」

translations.literal: After he died, the Emperor Taizu said to those around him: "When Gu died, it was like a tall pine falling of itself—not because I cut it down."
translations.idiomatic: After his death Emperor Taizu told those around him, "When Gu died, it was like a great pine toppling of its own weight—not because I felled it."

sentences.zh: 突呂不，字鐸袞，幼聰敏嗜學。

translations.literal: Tulubu, courtesy name Duogun, in youth was clever and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Tulubu, whose courtesy name was Duogun, was clever and devoted to learning from childhood.

sentences.zh: 事太祖見器重。

translations.literal: In serving the Emperor Taizu he was regarded with esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In serving Emperor Taizu he won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 及制契丹大字，突呂不贊成為多。

translations.literal: When the Khitan large script was devised, Tulubu contributed much to its completion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan large script was created, Tulubu contributed more than anyone else to bringing it to completion.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為文班林牙，領國子博士、知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he became Linya of the Civil Class, and concurrently held the posts of Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Linya of the Civil Class and concurrently served as Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

sentences.zh: 明年，受詔撰決獄法。

translations.literal: The next year he received an edict to compile the law on deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received an edict to draft the law on judicial decisions.

sentences.zh: 太祖略燕，詔與皇太子及王郁攻定州。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou together with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 師還至順州，幽州馬步軍指揮使王千率眾來襲，突呂不射其馬躓，擒之。

translations.literal: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led troops to attack; Tulubu shot his horse so that it stumbled and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led a raid; Tulubu shot his horse from under him and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 天贊二年，皇子堯骨為大元帥，突呂不為副，既克平州，進軍燕、趙，攻下曲陽、北平。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianzan, the prince Yaogu was Grand Marshal and Tulubu was his deputy; after they took Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianzan, Prince Yaogu served as grand marshal with Tulubu as his deputy; after taking Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.

sentences.zh: 至易州，易人來拒，逾濠而陣。

translations.literal: Reaching Yizhou, the people of Yi came out to resist and formed battle lines beyond the moat.
translations.idiomatic: At Yizhou the defenders came out to resist, forming their lines beyond the moat.

sentences.zh: 李景章出降，言城中人無鬥志。

translations.literal: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and said the people in the city had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and reported that the city had lost the will to fight.

sentences.zh: 大元帥將修攻具，突呂不諫曰：「我師遠來，人馬疲憊，勢不可久留。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal was about to prepare siege engines; Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has come from afar; men and horses are weary—the situation cannot allow a long stay.
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal was about to prepare siege engines when Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has marched far; men and horses are exhausted—we cannot afford to linger.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The assault was called off.

sentences.zh: 軍還，大元帥以其謀聞，太祖大悅，賜賚優渥。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Grand Marshal reported his counsel; the Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and bestowed generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the grand marshal reported his counsel to the throne; Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 車駕西征，突呂不與大元帥為先鋒，伐党項有功，太祖犒師水精山。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Tulubu and the Grand Marshal served as vanguard; in attacking the Tanguts they had merit, and the Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Shuijing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign Tulubu and the grand marshal led the vanguard; their attack on the Tanguts succeeded, and Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Crystal Mountain.

sentences.zh: 大元帥東歸，突呂不留屯西南部，復討党項，多獲而還。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal returned east; Tulubu remained to garrison the southwestern region, again attacked the Tanguts, took many captives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand marshal returned east, Tulubu remained to garrison the southwest, raided the Tanguts again, took many captives, and returned.

sentences.zh: 太祖東伐，大諲譔降而復叛，攻之，突呂不先登。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Taizu campaigned east, Dayinzan surrendered then rebelled again; in the attack Tulubu was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Taizu's eastern campaign, Dayinzan surrendered and then rebelled again; in the assault Tulubu was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 渤海平，承詔銘太祖功德於永興殿壁。

translations.literal: When Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe the Emperor Taizu's merit on the walls of the Yongxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe Emperor Taizu's achievements on the walls of the Hall of Everlasting Prosperity.

sentences.zh: 班師，已下州郡往往復叛，突呂不從大元帥攻破之。

translations.literal: On the withdrawal, prefectures and districts below often rebelled again; Tulubu followed the Grand Marshal in reducing them.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal many districts rebelled again; Tulubu followed the grand marshal in reducing them.

sentences.zh: 淳欽皇后稱制，有飛語中傷者，後怒，突呂不懼而亡。

translations.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, there were slanders that wounded him; the empress was angry, and Tulubu, in fear, fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, slanders reached her ears; enraged, she drove Tulubu to flee in fear.

sentences.zh: 太宗知其無罪，召還。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong knew he was guiltless and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong knew he was innocent and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 天顯三年，討烏古部，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took very many captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took a great many captives.

sentences.zh: 伐唐，以突呂不為左翼，攻唐軍霞沙寨，降之。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Tang, Tulubu was made left wing; he attacked the Tang army's Xiasha stockade and received its surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Tang he commanded the left wing, attacked the Tang garrison at Xiasha, and received its surrender.

sentences.zh: 十一年，送晉主石敬瑭入洛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及大冊，突呂不總禮儀事，加特進檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the great investiture he oversaw ritual affairs in general and was given Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand enthronement ceremony he oversaw all ritual affairs and was granted the ranks of Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 會同五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.

sentences.zh: 王郁，京兆萬年人，唐義武軍節度使處直之孽子。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, Tang Military Governor of Yiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, military governor of the Yiwu Army under Tang.

sentences.zh: 伯父處存鎮義武，卒，三軍推其子郜襲，處直為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: His uncle Chucun held Yiwu; when he died the three armies installed his son Gao as successor, and Chuzhi became Director of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Chucun had governed Yiwu; when he died the army installed his son Gao as successor, with Chuzhi as director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，梁王朱全忠攻定州，郜遣處直拒於沙河。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua, Liang King Zhu Quanzhong attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist at Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guanghua, Zhu Quanzhong of Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist him at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，入城逐郜，郜奔太原。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; they entered the city and drove out Gao, and Gao fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, they entered the city and drove Gao out; he fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 亂兵推處直為留後，遣人請事梁王。

translations.literal: The mutinous troops installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent men to request allegiance to the Liang king.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent envoys to submit to the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 梁與晉王克用絕好，表處直為義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Liang broke relations with Jin Prince Li Keyong and memorialized Chuzhi as Military Governor of Yiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liang broke with Li Keyong of Jin and memorialized Chuzhi as military governor of the Yiwu Army.

sentences.zh: 初，郜之亡也，郁從之。

translations.literal: At first, when Gao fled, Yu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao first fled, Yu went with him.

sentences.zh: 晉王克用妻以女，用為新州防禦使。

translations.literal: Jin Prince Li Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage and employed him as Defender of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Jin gave him his daughter in marriage and appointed him defender of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 處直料晉必討張文禮，鎮亡，則定不獨存，益自疑。

translations.literal: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely punish Zhang Wenli; if the commandery perished, Dingzhou could not stand alone, and he grew ever more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely move against Zhang Wenli; if the commandery fell, Dingzhou could not survive on its own, and his suspicions deepened.

sentences.zh: 陰使郁北導契丹入塞，以牽晉兵，且許為嗣。

translations.literal: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan into the passes, to tie down Jin's army, and also promised him the succession.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan across the border and tie down Jin's forces, promising him the succession as well.

sentences.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐失父心，得使，大喜。

translations.literal: Yu had himself fled to Jin and constantly feared losing his father's favor; when he received this mission he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had fled to Jin and constantly feared he had lost his father's favor; when this mission came he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 神冊六年，奉表送款，舉室來降，太祖以為養子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial offering allegiance; his whole household came to surrender, and the Emperor Taizu took him as an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial of allegiance and came over with his entire household; Emperor Taizu adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 未幾，郁兄都囚父，自為留後，帝遣郁從皇太子討之。

translations.literal: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and installed himself as acting governor; the emperor sent Yu to follow the heir apparent in punishing him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and made himself acting governor; the emperor sent Yu with the heir apparent to punish him.

sentences.zh: 至定州，都堅壁不出，掠居民而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Dingzhou, Du held fast behind the walls and would not come out; they plundered the inhabitants and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou, Du held the walls and refused to come out; they plundered the countryside and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，從皇太子攻鎮州，遇唐兵於定州，破之。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the heir apparent in attacking Zhenzhou; they met Tang troops at Dingzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed the heir apparent against Zhenzhou, met Tang forces at Dingzhou, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 天贊二年秋，郁及阿古只略地燕、趙，攻下磁窯務。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi overran the lands of Yan and Zhao and took Ciyaowu.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi raided Yan and Zhao and captured Ciyaowu.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平渤海，戰有功，加同政事門下平章事，改崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Following the Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, he had merit in battle and was made Associate Director of the Secretariat with the rank of Grand Councilor, then transferred to Military Governor of Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, distinguished himself in battle, was made associate director of the Secretariat with the rank of grand councilor, and was then appointed military governor of the Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，郁與妻會葬，其妻泣訴於淳欽皇后，求歸鄉國，許之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept and appealed to Empress Chunqin, asking to return to their native land, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept before Empress Chunqin and begged to return home, and the empress granted her request.

sentences.zh: 郁奏曰：「臣本唐主之婿，主已被弒，此行夫妻豈能相保？

translations.literal: Yu memorialized: "This subject was originally the son-in-law of the Tang ruler; my lord has already been assassinated—on this journey how can husband and wife protect each other?
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial: "I was once the son-in-law of a Tang ruler; my lord has already been murdered—on this journey how can my wife and I keep each other safe?

sentences.zh: 願常侍太后。

translations.literal: I wish to attend the empress dowager constantly.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to remain in constant attendance upon the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 」後喜曰：「漢人中，惟王郎最忠孝。

translations.literal: " The empress rejoiced: "Among the Han, only Lord Wang is most loyal and filial.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress was delighted: "Among the Han, none is more loyal and filial than Lord Wang.

sentences.zh: 」以太祖嘗與李克用約為兄弟故也。

translations.literal: " This was because the Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: " This was because Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 尋加政事令。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Director of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was additionally appointed director of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 還宜州，卒。

translations.literal: He returned to Yizhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 耶律圖魯窘，字阿魯隱，肅祖子洽瑽之孫，勇而有謀略。

translations.literal: Yelu Tulujiong, courtesy name Aluyin, was the grandson of Qiazhen, son of Emperor Suzu; he was brave and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Tulujiong, whose courtesy name was Aluyin, was the grandson of Qiazhen, a son of Emperor Suzu; he was courageous and resourceful in counsel.

sentences.zh: 太宗立晉之役，其父敵魯古為五院夷離堇，歿於兵，帝即以其職授圖魯窘。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's campaign to establish Jin, his father Dilugu was Yilijin of the Five Yuan Divisions and died in battle; the emperor at once gave Tulujiong his post.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's campaign to establish the Later Jin state, his father Dilugu served as chieftain of the Five Yuan Divisions and died in battle; the emperor at once gave Tulujiong his father's post.

sentences.zh: 會同元年，改北院大王，嘗屏左右與議大事，占對合上意。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huitong he was made King of the Northern Court; he would dismiss attendants to discuss great affairs, and his responses matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huitong he was made king of the Northern Court; he would dismiss his attendants to discuss weighty matters, and his counsel always matched the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 從討石重貴，杜重威擁十萬餘眾拒滹沱橋，力戰數日，不得進。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Shi Chonggui, Du Chongwei held more than a hundred thousand men to block the Hutuo bridge; they fought fiercely for several days but could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Shi Chonggui, Du Chongwei held more than a hundred thousand men at the Hutuo bridge; after days of fierce fighting the army could not break through.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「兩軍爭渡，人馬疲矣，計安出？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The two armies contend for the crossing; men and horses are weary—what plan should be adopted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Both armies are fighting for the crossing; men and horses are exhausted—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」諸將請緩師，為後圖，帝然之。

translations.literal: " The generals asked to slow the army and plan for later; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals urged slowing the advance to regroup; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 圖魯窘厲色進曰：「臣愚竊以為陛下樂於安逸，則謹守四境可也；

translations.literal: Tulujiong advanced with stern countenance and said: "This foolish subject ventures to think that if Your Majesty delights in ease, then strictly guarding the four borders would suffice;
translations.idiomatic: Tulujiong stepped forward with a stern expression and said, "Your humble servant ventures to think that if Your Majesty delights in ease, then guarding the four borders is enough;

sentences.zh: 既欲擴大疆宇，出師遠攻，詎能無廑聖慮。

translations.literal: if you wish to expand territory and send the army on distant attack, how can there be no anxious imperial deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: but if you wish to expand the realm and send the army on distant campaigns, how can Your Majesty not weigh every consequence with care?

sentences.zh: 若中路而止，適為賊利，則必陷南京，夷屬邑。

translations.literal: If we halt halfway, that would only profit the enemy; then the Southern Capital would surely fall and dependent districts be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If we halt halfway, we only strengthen the enemy; the Southern Capital will fall and our dependent districts will be laid waste.

sentences.zh: 若此，則爭戰未已，吾民無奠枕之期矣。

translations.literal: If so, fighting would not cease and our people would have no time to lay their heads on pillows in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Then the fighting will never end, and our people will never know a night of peaceful sleep.

sentences.zh: 且彼步我騎，何慮不克！

translations.literal: Moreover, they are infantry and we are cavalry—what worry is there of not conquering!
translations.idiomatic: They fight on foot and we fight on horseback—why should we fear defeat?

sentences.zh: 況漢人足力弱而行緩，如選輕銳騎先絕其餉道，則事蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Han have weak legs and slow marching; if we choose light, elite cavalry first to cut off their supply route, then the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Han march slowly on weak legs; send light, elite cavalry to cut their supply lines first, and the matter cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」帝喜曰：「國強則其人賢，海巨則其魚大。

translations.literal: " The emperor rejoiced: "When the state is strong its men are worthy; when the sea is vast its fish are large.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rejoiced: "When a state is strong, its men are worthy; when the sea is vast, its fish are large.

sentences.zh: 」於是塞其餉道，數出師以牽撓其勢，重威果降如言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they blocked their supply route and sent out troops several times to harass their strength; Chongwei indeed surrendered as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: " They blocked the enemy supply lines and sent out repeated raids to harry their forces; Chongwei surrendered exactly as Tulujiong had predicted.

sentences.zh: 以功獲賜甚厚。

translations.literal: For his merit he received very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 明年春，卒軍中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 論曰：神冊初元，將相大臣拔起風塵之中，翼扶王運，以任職取名者，固一時之材，亦由太祖推誠禦下，不任獨斷，用能總攬群策而為之用歟！

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Shence, generals, ministers, and great officials were raised from the dust of turmoil to wing and support the royal fortune. Those who gained fame through office were indeed talents of their time, but it was also because the Emperor Taizu treated subordinates with sincerity, did not rely on solitary decisions, and thus could gather all strategies and put them to use!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: At the opening of the Shence era, generals and ministers rose from the turmoil of the age to support the royal enterprise. Men who won renown through office were indeed talents of their day, yet it was also because Emperor Taizu dealt sincerely with his subordinates, refused to decide everything alone, and so could gather every counsel and put it to use.

sentences.zh: 其投天隙而列功庸，至有心腹、耳目、手足之喻，豈偶然哉！

translations.literal: That they seized Heaven's openings and ranked their achievements, even to the metaphors of heart, eyes and ears, and hands and feet—was this accidental?
translations.idiomatic: That they seized Heaven's openings and won their places of honor, even to the point of being called the ruler's heart, eyes, ears, hands, and feet—could that have been mere chance?

sentences.zh: 討党項，走敵魯，平剌葛，定渤海，功亦偉矣。

translations.literal: In punishing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were also grand.
translations.idiomatic: In subduing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were likewise magnificent.

sentences.zh: 若默記治獄不冤，頗德持論不撓，延徽立經陳紀，紹勛秉節而死，圖魯窘料敵制勝，豈器博者無近用，道長者其功遠歟？

translations.literal: As for Moji in governing cases without injustice, Pode in holding to argument without yielding, Yanhui in establishing classics and setting forth institutions, Shaoxun in holding to integrity unto death, and Tulujiong in gauging the enemy and controlling victory—can those whose vessels are broad have no near use, and those whose Way is long have achievements that reach far?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Kang Moji, who judged cases without injustice; Pode, who held to his principles without yielding; Han Yanhui, who established institutions and set forth the laws; Shaoxun, who died holding to his integrity; and Tulujiong, who read the enemy and secured victory—are men of broad talent useless in the present, and men of far-reaching vision rewarded only in the long run?

sentences.zh: 稱為佐命，固宜。

translations.literal: To call them assistants in establishing the mandate was surely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To call them founders of the dynasty was only fitting.
